note: tools/run_job.py data/jobs/nominal_C.json --sim --scenario realistic --seed N --compare (camera loop vs dead reckoning, strict grasp) and --no-camera --lenient-grasp (dead reckoning to the end), seeds 1-3, plus --scenario slip --seed 1 (camera loop); the rows collected with run_job.sim_once (2026-10-06, the C with ARES INSIDE: legs A 10 / B 7 / C 5 stones, A on ARES's right and C on its left at 580 mm, B in front at 840 mm, ARES at heading 0 throughout, 94 stones, stacked pick-up station; looks checked against ARES and a full magazine, leg A's boards at u 300 / 700 / 1100 / 1700). The true ARES path is checked against the legs, plates and the station table (mauer.simworld floor check).
discussion: - Camera loop, realistic: 94/94 seated in every seed (12/12 half stones), horizontal error max 3.84-3.97 mm, dominated by the errors outside the loop (1 mm UR-mount error and 1 mm holder scatter on the deck magazine, WorldErrors.realistic): the `slip` scenario gives 94/94 within 0.43 mm (seed 1). The C with ARES outside (same day, 840 mm): max 3.88-4.01 mm - the side walls with their 600 mm board baseline cost nothing measurable.
- ARES: 64-69 moves and 5.7-5.8 min of driving per run (outside: 9.6-9.8 min), 6 station trips; the rotations are the turns to and from the dock - between the stops ARES only translates.

- True ARES path (camera loop): no move touches a leg, plate or the table in the 4 runs; smallest gap to an obstacle 67-68 mm realistic, 67 mm slip (ARES 110 mm from the plates of the leg it builds; the stop limits keep it 50 mm from the other legs' plates).

- Dead reckoning stops at a station pick (the gripper misses stone s00l2; 30, 30, 15 stones placed); with a lenient gripper the 94 stones miss the pins by up to 222 mm (0, 15, 2 seated), 79, 79, 72 of the 79 stones moved station -> magazine land off their holders (up to 121 mm) and ARES drives up to 27 mm onto the plates (plate W0) - the reference case without the camera.
